brief: JPM's Retail Radar reports the Fed unanimously hiked 25bps to 3.75-4%, with dot-plot guidance implying one more hike this year. JPM argues a shallow hiking cycle, essentially reversing last year's insurance cuts, should be manageable for equities if earnings stay strong, and that equities can withstand 10y yields trending toward 6% given an inverted-U relationship with S&P multiples. Against that backdrop, retail flows turned materially weaker last week (2nd percentile overall, ETF inflows at 1-year lows, single-name flows at the 12th percentile), totaling $2.5B versus a $6.8B 12-month average, as Rates-factor crowding rose to match Momentum crowding. Retail rotated defensively, buying only Staples ex-Mag7 while selling Industrials, Communications and Tech, and kept buying all seven Mag7 names led by NVDA. A reignited AI-safety debate revived the Semis-vs-Software narrative Monday: Software outperformed Semiconductors by about 8 percentage points, retail sold non-Mag7 semis like AMAT while still buying NVDA, and it sold the security-software cohort (PANW, CRWD, FTNT, NOW) even as JPM analysts turned more bullish on those names post-2Q.
